content: It can be used on its own or in combination with other medications. Prazosin belongs to a class of drugs known as alpha-blockers. It works by relaxing the blood vessels, which allows blood to flow more easily throughout the body. Prazosin is available in capsule form and is taken orally. It is typically taken two or three times a day at evenly spaced intervals. When taking prazosin for the first time, it is recommended to take it before going to bed. You should carefully follow the instructions on your prescription label and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. It is important to take prazosin exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. You should continue taking it even if you feel well, and you should not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. If you are prescribed prazosin for any of these conditions, discuss the potential risks with your doctor. Prazosin may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting prazosin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to prazosin or any related medications, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, or terazosin. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Notify your doctor if you have narcolepsy, a history of prostate cancer, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking prazosin, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking prazosin. Additionally, if you require eye surgery during or after treatment, let your doctor know that you are currently or have previously taken prazosin. Be aware that prazosin may cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing hazardous tasks for 24 hours after your first dose or after a dose increase. Consult your doctor about the safe consumption of alcohol while taking prazosin, as alcohol can exacerbate its side effects. To minimize these effects, rise slowly from a lying position and rest your feet on the floor before standing. If you experience these symptoms, sit or lie down. These effects may also occur after consuming alcohol, standing for long periods, exercising, or in hot weather. If the symptoms persist, contact your doctor. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations, which may include reducing your salt intake. If you miss a dose of prazosin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. If you miss two or more doses, consult your doctor. Prazosin may cause side effects. Minor side effects include weakness, tiredness, headache, and nausea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing, a fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, or a painful erection lasting several hours. If you experience any of these, seek medical attention immediately. Store prazosin in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include drowsiness, decreased reflexes, dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking prazosin. Inform your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are taking prazosin before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Prazosin is sold under the brand name Minipress®.
